name: Arizona 29-card Pitch
description: Arizona 29-card Pitch is a specialized regional evolution of the classic American game Pitch (Setback). It uses a condensed 29-card deck and incorporates an unbeatable Joker into the trump hierarchy. Played in partnerships, it rewards both the capture of legendary cards (High, Low, Jack) and the strategic management of a 5-card kitty.

overview.description: Arizona 29-card Pitch is a specialized regional evolution of the classic American game Pitch (Setback). It uses a condensed 29-card deck and incorporates an unbeatable Joker into the trump hierarchy. Played in partnerships, it rewards both the capture of legendary cards (High, Low, Jack) and the strategic management of a 5-card kitty.

history.origins: Developed in the Southwestern United States as a faster, more intense version of the standard 52-card Partnership Pitch. The use of the '6' as the low card instead of the '2' is a regional hallmark.
timeline: 1800s: Pitch (Setback) becomes popular in back-woods America.
mid-20th C.: Arizona players standardize the 29-card 'short deck' format.
Present: Remains a popular 'Social Club' game in Arizona and neighboring states.
history.cultural: In Arizona, this game is often preferred over standard 'Seven Up' for its predictive bidding and the power of the 'Kitty' exchange.
history.evolution: The transition to a 29-card deck was likely an adaptation to make the Joker (a common 53rd card) more central to the gameplay, as it acts as a 'Middle-Trump'.

setup.players: 4 players in two partnerships (North-South vs East-West).
setup.deck: 29 cards: Ace, King, Queen, Jack, Ten, Nine, Six of each suit, plus one Joker. Remove 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, and 8 from a standard deck.
setup.dealing: Each player is dealt 6 cards in batches of 3. The 5 remaining cards are placed face down as the 'Kitty'.

rules.objective: The bidding team must earn at least as many points as they bid. Points are scored for High, Low, Jack, Joker, and Game.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Bidding**: Starting left of the dealer, players bid for the right to 'Pitch' (name trump). Bids range from 1 to 5. 2. **The Kitty**: The high bidder takes the 5-card kitty and discards 5 cards to return to a 6-card hand. 3. **The Pitch**: The high bidder leads the first card; the suit of this card is trumps. 4. **Trump Hierarchy**: A (High), K, Q, J, Joker, 10, 9, 6 (Low). 5. **Trick Play**: Must follow suit if possible; else any card. Highest trump wins the trick; if no trump, highest card of led suit wins. 6. **Scoring**: At hand's end, count points.
keyRules: High (1 pt): Winning or holding the highest trump in play (Ace).
Low (1 pt): Winning or holding the lowest trump in play (Six).
Jack (1 pt): Capturing the Jack of trumps in a trick.
Joker (1 pt): Capturing the Joker in a trick.
Game (1 pt): Winning the highest total value of pip-cards (A=4, K=3, Q=2, J=1, 10=10).

strategy.basic: If you win the bid, use the kitty to 'flush' your hand of non-trump suits. Keeping only trumps and high cards (Aces/Tens) is the path to winning the 'Game' point.
strategy.intermediate: Trump Pulling: If you have the Ace of trumps, lead it early to draw out the opponents' Joker and Jack. This 'purifies' the remaining trumps for your partner.
strategy.advanced: Defense: If the opponents bid 5 (the maximum), your only goal is to 'Set' them by stealing just one of the 5 points. Focus your play on capturing the Joker or the Jack specifically.
tips: The Nine and Six are often overlooked, but they contribute to the 'Game' point count if they capture a Ten.
Joker Management: The Joker is a 'wild' trump that ranks between the Jack and the Ten. Use it to kill a King or Queen lead if the Jack is already gone.

variations.name: Standard Partnership Pitch
variations.description: Played with the full 52-card deck (minus Joker). High to Low is A to 2.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: This variation is described textually; specific engine overrides for the full-deck version are not yet modeled.

variations.name: Flat Pitch
variations.description: No kitty is dealt; players play only with the 6 cards originally dealt.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Flat Pitch removes the kitty but keeps the same core flow; engine-level override values will be added when that variant is modeled.

scoring.description: Pitch uses a 'Setback' scoring system where failing a bid subtracts from your total.
scoring.winCondition: Usually played to a target score of 21 or 31 points.

synthesis.shortDescription: Experience the high-stakes world of Arizona 29-card Pitch. Use the kitty to perfect your hand, leverage the Joker to smash your opponents, and don't get 'Set Back'!
